works.name: Edelmore Reader
works.hero: A book that reads itself to you — on your own machine.
works.personal_stake: For a kid who hears stories better than she reads them — and for anyone who wants reading to feel like the thing it used to be.
works.short_description: A self-hosted read-along EPUB reader that feels like a real book. Upload an EPUB or pick from a built-in library of public-domain children's books; the book opens where you left off, a songbird in the margin reads it aloud in a warm voice, and each word glows softly as it's spoken. Pages turn when the narration reaches the end of the page; the book remembers your place. Built for kids who hear stories better than they read them. Sibling project to Edelmore Diary, sharing its book metaphor, narration stack, and cottage-core identity; gated on the diary's refactor into shared modules. Seed committed, no code yet.
substantive_description: Read-along ebook readers exist, and the technical problem — parsing EPUB, generating speech, highlighting words as they're spoken — is solved many times over. What none of them solve is the experience: every one feels like reading software, utilitarian and clinical, with no spatial sense of where you are in the book. For a kid with ataxia, dyslexia, attention differences, or just a preference for being read to, the gap between 'software that reads at you' and 'a book that's also reading itself to you' is the gap between using a tool and inhabiting an experience.

Edelmore Reader's differentiator isn't the technology — it's that the book metaphor is the product. The page turn, the warm serif typography, the soft green word-glow; the audio narration is one ingredient inside a larger reading experience, not the feature. It is the same warmth the diary built for writing, applied to published content — accessibility tools made to look like things people actually want to use.

relationships.note: The sibling fork: reuses the diary's book metaphor, narration stack, visual identity, and deployment pattern; swaps the content model (diary entries → book chapters).
